pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: In your own words: what *is* a git branch, and why do teams work on branches instead of committing straight to main?
expected_points: a branch is a movable name pointing at a commit — not a copy of the project
creating one is nearly free; committing moves the branch you are on
main stays the always-working version while experiments live safely elsewhere
parallel lines of work can exist and dead ends are cheap to discard

questions.prompt: Walk me through taking a change from a branch into main: the commands, and when git fast-forwards versus creates a merge commit.
expected_points: git switch -c to create/switch, commit there, git switch main, git merge <branch>
fast-forward: main did not move since branching, so the tag just slides forward — no new commit
merge commit: both sides gained commits, so git makes a commit with two parents

questions.prompt: What is a merge conflict, and what exactly do you do when git reports one?
expected_points: both branches changed the same lines, so git cannot choose and pauses the merge
git writes both versions into the file fenced by <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> markers
edit the file to the final text, remove the markers, git add, then git commit to finish
git merge --abort backs out; a conflict is a question, not breakage

questions.prompt: What is a remote, and what do push and pull actually move?
expected_points: a remote is another full copy of the repository known by a nickname, origin by convention
it can be GitHub or even a plain folder — the commands are identical
push uploads commits to the remote branch; uncommitted edits never leave your machine
pull is fetch (download new commits, update origin/main) plus merge into your branch

questions.prompt: People say 'main' about three different things: your main, the server's main, and origin/main. Untangle them.
expected_points: local branch main lives in your repo and moves when you commit
the remote branch main lives in origin's repo and moves when anyone pushes
origin/main is a remote-tracking branch: your read-only bookmark of the server's main from the last time you talked to it
origin/main can be stale — it only updates on push, pull, or fetch

questions.prompt: Walk through the pull-request flow from starting a change to it landing on main. Which parts are git and which are GitHub?
expected_points: branch, commit, and push the branch — all git
opening the PR, review discussion, and the merge button happen on GitHub
pushing more commits to the same branch updates the open PR
after the server-side merge, everyone git pulls main; the point is review and a written record

questions.prompt: A teammate pushed to main an hour ago; you have run no git commands since. Where does your origin/main point right now, and what two things happen when you run git pull?
expected_points: origin/main still points at the old commit — nothing updates it until you contact the remote
pull first fetches, moving origin/main to the teammate's commit
then it merges origin/main into your local main
